page: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v7 is a member of the Dldsv7 server family, utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system includes 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 5669 GB, and the server does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 100098.18 and a PassMark CPU score of 108246.31, both placing in the top tiers. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), contribute to a PassMark extended instructions score of 125494.83. Memory read-only bandwidth for small cached blocks reaches a top-tier 7403.16 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write speeds are measured at 349.97 GB/sec and 137.53 GB/sec respectively.

This configuration is optimized for compute-heavy workloads that require high CPU clock speeds and substantial local storage but do not demand high memory density. The 2.0 GB of RAM per core represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications, though the server excels in database operations, achieving 33207.86 operations per second on PassMark and 159.81 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. It is also suited for static web serving, showing a throughput of 150.35 GB/sec, and CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing where it achieves top-tier token generation rates across small, medium, and large models.
